title: AlphaFold homodimer predictions link truncation to different interface outcomes
summary: The May 9, 2026 preprint version compared 5,168 canonical/truncated human homodimer prediction pairs using AlphaFold-Multimer structures and interface-confidence scores. Among 234 pairs with high-confidence canonical homodimers, it classified 132 as conserved, 61 as interface-ablated and 41 as partially destabilized. These are computational classifications, without biochemical or cellular confirmation of the specific dimers. The later deposited abstract retains these headline proportions but revises interpretations of apparent interface emergence; those emergence and disorder claims are outside this entry.

evidence.tested: Computational comparison of 5168 AlphaFold-predicted canonical/truncated homodimer pairs, including confidence-tier classifications and within-study robustness analyses; the represented three-class counts refer to the234 high-confidence canonical pairs.
evidence.unknown: No binding-affinity, cellular-complex or biochemical confirmation is established for individual predicted dimers. The later deposited abstract changes interpretation of apparent emergence; this entry represents only the common core classes documented in the May9v1.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts/scored homodimer interfaces; comparisons of canonical and truncated-isoform structures yield the represented interface classes.

source_review.scope: May9v1 primary PDF abstract, Results class counts, AlphaFold-Multimer Methods and limitations; comparison with current publisher-deposited Crossref abstract to bound version-dependent claims.
